---
title: "Language selector"
---

Askr 0.10.0 adds an optional site language selector through `askr.languages`.
Askr places the current-tab links in a Header control beside the theme and other
tools. The control stays in the Header on narrow screens, independently of
Areas. With no configuration, Askr adds no language control and all other
defaults remain unchanged.

## Configure languages

Set `current` to the code for this language project's pages. Each entry
provides a unique `code`, display `label` and exact destination `href`:

```yaml
askr:
  languages:
    current: zh-TW
    items:
      - code: zh-TW
        label: 繁體中文
        href: https://docs.example.org/
      - code: en
        label: English
        href: https://docs.example.org/en/
```

Provide at least two entries. Codes and labels must be nonempty scalar values,
and codes must be unique. Each `href` must be an absolute HTTPS URL or a
domain-root path such as `/en/`; protocol-relative paths such as `//other.org`
and destinations containing whitespace are rejected during rendering.
Set `current` explicitly in each language project's configuration; Askr does
not infer it from the current URL.

## Bilingual Gallery example

The English site remains at `/askr/`, and its Traditional Chinese edition is a
separate Quarto project at `/askr/zh-TW/`. Each site has its own navigation and
search. The root project sets `current: en`; the Chinese project sets
`current: zh-TW`. Selecting a language opens its configured homepage, not an
automatically paired page in the other language.

Run `quarto render` from the repository root to build both sites. The build
stages the shared Askr extension, images and bibliography for the child project;
the three executable examples live once in root `_includes/` and are included
by both sites. For a local preview, serve the output under the `/askr/` path or
configure local selector destinations; the published domain-root links do not
match a prefix-less preview URL.

Askr puts the configured `href` on a normal link, so the browser opens it in the
current tab. It uses each code as both `lang` and `hreflang`, and marks the
current item visually and with `aria-current`. The button shows the accessible
name and tooltip `Language: <current label>`; the current language is also
visible in the menu.

Askr does not guess URLs, pair translated pages, remember language choices,
change search, or translate content. If your native navbar already contains
language links, remove those duplicates after configuring the Askr selector;
Askr leaves authored navbar tools in place.

The selector uses Quarto's bundled Bootstrap dropdown behavior for keyboard
navigation, Escape and outside-click dismissal. Without JavaScript, the
configuration stays inert and no button is shown.
